classes.name: Extrema_ExtPElC
classes.summary: It calculates all the distances between a point and an elementary curve. These distances can be minimum or maximum.

constructors.name: constructor
constructors.signature: (P: gp_Pnt, C: gp_Lin, Tol: number, Uinf: number, Usup: number)
constructors.comment: Calculates the extremum distance between the point P and the segment [Uinf,Usup] of the line C.

constructors.name: constructor
constructors.signature: (P: gp_Pnt, C: gp_Circ, Tol: number, Uinf: number, Usup: number)
constructors.comment: Calculates the 2 extremum distances between the point P and the segment [Uinf,Usup] of the circle C. Tol is used to determine if P is on the axis of the circle or if an extremum is on an endpoint of the segment. If P is on the axis of the circle, there are infinite solution then IsDone(me)=False. The conditions on the Uinf and Usup are:<= Uinf <= 2.*PI and Usup > Uinf. If Usup > Uinf + 2.*PI, then only the solutions in the range [Uinf,Uinf+2.*PI[ are computed.

constructors.name: constructor
constructors.signature: (P: gp_Pnt, C: gp_Elips, Tol: number, Uinf: number, Usup: number)
constructors.comment: Calculates the 4 extremum distances between the point P and the segment [Uinf,Usup] of the ellipse C. Tol is used to determine if the point is on the axis of the ellipse and if the major radius is equal to the minor radius or if an extremum is on an endpoint of the segment. If P is on the axis of the ellipse, there are infinite solution then IsDone(me)=False. The conditions on the Uinf and Usup are:<= Uinf <= 2.*PI and Usup > Uinf. If Usup > Uinf + 2.*PI, then only the solutions in the range [Uinf,Uinf+2.*PI[ are computed.

constructors.name: constructor
constructors.signature: (P: gp_Pnt, C: gp_Hypr, Tol: number, Uinf: number, Usup: number)
constructors.comment: Calculates the extremum distances between the point P and the segment [Uinf,Usup] of the hyperbola C. Tol is used to determine if two solutions u and v are identical; the condition is: dist(C(u),C(v)) < Tol.

constructors.name: constructor
constructors.signature: (P: gp_Pnt, C: gp_Parab, Tol: number, Uinf: number, Usup: number)
constructors.comment: Calculates the 4 extremum distances between the point P and the segment [Uinf,Usup] of the parabola C. Tol is used to determine if two solutions u and v are identical; the condition is: dist(C(u),C(v)) < Tol.

classes.name: Extrema_FuncPSDist
classes.summary:
Functional for search of extremum of the square Euclidean distance between point P and surface S, starting from approximate solution (u0, v0).
The class inherits {@link math_MultipleVarFunctionWithGradient | `math_MultipleVarFunctionWithGradient`} and thus is intended for use in {@link math_BFGS | `math_BFGS`} algorithm.
The criteria is: F = SquareDist(P, S(u, v)) - > min
The first derivative are: F1(u,v) = (S(u,v) - P) * Su F2(u,v) = (S(u,v) - P) * Sv
Su and Sv are first derivatives of the surface, * symbol means dot product.

classes.name: Extrema_FuncPSNorm
classes.summary:
Functional for search of extremum of the distance between point P and surface S, starting from approximate solution (u0, v0).
The class inherits {@link math_FunctionSetWithDerivatives | `math_FunctionSetWithDerivatives`} and thus is intended for use in {@link math_FunctionSetRoot | `math_FunctionSetRoot`} algorithm .
Denoting derivatives of the surface S(u,v) by u and v, respectively, as Su and Sv, the two functions to be nullified are:
F1(u,v) = (S - P) * Su F2(u,v) = (S - P) * Sv
The derivatives of the functional are:
Duf1(u,v) = Su^2 + (S-P) * Suu; Dvf1(u,v) = Su * Sv + (S-P) * Suv Duf2(u,v) = Sv * Su + (S-P) * Suv = Dvf1 Dvf2(u,v) = Sv^2 + (S-P) * Svv
Here * denotes scalar product, and ^2 is square power.
